We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Developer Advocate. In this role, you’ll play a core part in improving our developer experience, particularly our documentation and example projects. You’ll dive deep into where users are getting stuck and ship what they need to succeed. You’ll also help drive acquisition of our technical, self-serve customers by creating and presenting engaging content online and in-person, especially at developer meetups and conferences across the globe. This role is perfect for someone who can create compelling technical content and is energized by connecting with developers face-to-face. REQUIREMENTS - You love attending, organizing, and speaking at developer events. - You're able to tailor messaging for different audiences and build strong networks with developers, startup accelerators, and VCs alike. - A strong full-stack engineering skillset with extensive experience working with AI tools. - The ability to come up with great ideas for tutorials, build working demos, and create high-quality blog posts, videos and talks. - A passion for writing engaging technical content. - A product-minded approach to content: you understand metrics, speak to users, decide what to build/write based on needs, and double down on what works. LOCATION This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Bangalore, Dublin, London, New York, San Francisco, Tokyo, and Warsaw. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

items.title: Lead Data Engineer
items.description: We’re looking for an Lead Data Engineer to join the Paid Media Insights team within Better Collective. The Domanin Paid media is where the data has to pay off. We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut and which markets get budget comes out of this team’s models. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, stitched into one user-level view of what a click was worth. That model exists and it works. The most demanding domain on our platform: the most sources, the fastest schema churn, the shortest patience for a late table. We want the engineer who owns it. Where this role sits A central platform team sets the how. You set the what. A central team owns the platform - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a spoke in that hub and spoke organisation, building on it. The split is deliberate: the platform team decides how data is produced, you decide what paid media produces and own everything we run. No new stack to build, and no year lost to plumbing a central team should solve once. Be a demanding customer: when a golden path does not fit paid media, push for it to change rather than quietly building around it. You report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial, CRM and platform teams. What you will own Every data job in paid media. All of it. Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the 07:30 incident before the spend review. A paid media model that is wrong or late is yours, not the platform team’s - that accountability is the core of the role. The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on. Ingestion of paid media sources on the platform’s framework: which sources, which schemas, and what happens when a network changes its API unannounced. The domain’s models, from staging to the marts analysts query, plus the semantic meaning on top. Nobody at the centre can define a qualified signup in paid media. You can. Reverse ETL into the ad platforms, so conversion data lands where it changes bidding. The handover, taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs for us. What you will lead A group of engineers, and the standard they build to Technical lead for the data engineers in Paid Media Insights: setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing, unblocking, and growing them by giving away the interesting problems. Shaping the domain’s roadmap with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams. Representing paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science. Hands-on technical leadership, not a step away from building. You will be in the code. What we’re looking for More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working. You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. You want the pager as well as the model, and would rather own a domain end to end than hand off the consequences. You break complex systems into simple parts. Attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, dozens of disagreeing source APIs - you hold that and still hand the business something it can reason about. You raise the people around you. Colleagues come to you for technical advice. You review generously, give feedback that lands, and would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does. You work well with a platform team. items.title: Data Science Tech Lead Manager, Model Experience
items.location_text: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company's mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world. You'll be the senior data science leader for Model Experience and a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders. Working where frontier AI research reaches the public, you'll help shape model roadmap and launch decisions, bringing a point of view on how users experience our models and what good looks like beyond benchmark scores. As a tech lead manager, you'll also hire and manage a team of data scientists, setting their agenda, personally leading the highest-stakes analyses, and raising the bar for how data shapes model and product decisions. Responsibilities: Act as a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders, helping shape model roadmap priorities, launch decisions, and the major bets the team makes Set the data science agenda for Model Experience, deciding where the team can have the most impact on model development and launch decisions and what it should deprioritize Hire, manage, and develop a team of data scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions Frame the most important and ambiguous questions about model quality and user experience, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction Define how Model Experience measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks across external products and internal testing that align teams and leadership on what matters Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Model Experience, including where launches lack a clean A/B test, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses Turn complex analyses of model and user behavior into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Model Experience needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our models and products evolve You may be a good fit if you: Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a product or research area at significant scale Have 3+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction, hiring, and developing senior data scientists Have been a trusted partner to senior product, research, and business leaders, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision Bring strong product sense and business judgment, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others' technical work Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress Care about the company's mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI Strong candidates may also have: Experience with AI/ML products, large language models, or developer tools in the AI/ML ecosystem Experience as a tech lead manager or player-coach, balancing hands-on technical work with people management Experience building or scaling a data science team in a fast-growing organization Experience working closely with Product or Research teams, especially on LLM or AI products Comfort working with unstructured data The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $380,000 — $460,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. This work brings together commercial, technical, strategy, and operations teams to secure and develop the sites and capacity needed for large-scale compute deployment. items.title: Mechanical Lead
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's data center construction teams work with engineering, supply chain, safety, quality, commissioning and operations partners to deliver the infrastructure that supports our computing needs. Mechanical delivery brings together cooling equipment, plant, piping and controls interfaces so that systems are installed, tested and ready for commissioning. About the Role As a Mechanical Lead, you will lead mechanical field delivery for data center construction, including cooling infrastructure, mechanical yards, piping and data hall fit-out. You will oversee general contractors, specialist installers and service providers, combining practical mechanical expertise with hands-on field leadership. Your focus will be safe installation, contractor performance, coordinated interfaces and complete evidence for commissioning and operational handover. Key Responsibilities - Manage mechanical contractors, equipment and piping installers, and general-contractor interfaces against approved scope, schedule and quality requirements. - Oversee installation readiness and delivery of cooling plant, pumps, heat rejection equipment, air handling, piping and applicable liquid-cooling infrastructure. - Coordinate equipment placement, pipe routing, supports, access and maintainability with structural, electrical, controls and hardware teams. - Review contractor work plans, constructability, submittals, RFIs and change proposals; resolve field issues with the responsible engineering teams. - Oversee pressure testing, flushing, cleaning and inspection records; verify completion, defect closure and commissioning readiness. - Support commissioning specialists with mechanical startup and system tests, corrective work and complete as-built, operating and maintenance documentation. - Set contractor priorities, review staffing and progress, identify constraints early and coordinate recovery actions with construction leadership. - Maintain clear progress, risk and change reporting, with accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams. Qualifications - Substantial mechanical construction, installation, field engineering or startup experience in data center cooling or comparable critical facilities. - Demonstrated leadership of mechanical contractors or crews, including coordination across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority. - Practical knowledge of cooling, ventilation, hydronic and pumping systems, heat rejection, piping cleanliness and vendor startup requirements. - Ability to review drawings, specifications, submittals, work methods and controls narratives for constructability and installation readiness. - Experience coordinating inspection, pressure testing, flushing, cleaning, balancing prerequisites and controls checkout. - Ability to interpret test results and deficiency records with commissioning specialists and coordinate corrective work, retesting and turnover evidence. - Clear communication and sound judgment when coordinating power, controls, startup and testing dependencies or escalating safety and delivery risks. - Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills - Owner-side or specialist-contractor experience with high-density data center cooling, liquid cooling or phased cooling-system startup. - Experience with integrated systems testing, factory or site acceptance activities, and digital commissioning or field-reporting tools. - Relevant mechanical trade, controls, balancing or commissioning qualifications, or professional engineering credentials. items.title: Fire Protection Engineer
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners. The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations. About the Role We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses. - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases. - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems. - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems. - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks. - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction. - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems. - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities. - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards. - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements. - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems. - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments. - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes. - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems. - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results. - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders. - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation. - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous. - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs. - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure. - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis. - Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces. - Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites. items.title: HSE and Portfolio Performance Lead
items.description: About the Team The Data Center Build and Delivery team develops the infrastructure that supports OpenAI’s research and products. We work with engineering, construction partners and Operations to deliver safe, reliable facilities at scale. As our portfolio grows, consistent health, safety and environmental practices and clear performance measures help teams identify risks early and deliver sites that are ready to operate. About the Role We are looking for an HSE and Portfolio Performance Lead to strengthen health, safety and environmental oversight and performance management across our data center construction portfolio. You will help sites meet applicable OSHA standards and other HSE requirements, from construction through commissioning and handoff to Operations. You will work across site teams, delivery partners and central functions to establish practical expectations, verify execution and turn portfolio data into action. This role combines hands-on HSE expertise with a portfolio view of contractor performance, risk and operational readiness. Key Responsibilities - Develop a consistent portfolio HSE framework covering contractor expectations, risk assessments, field verification, training and escalation, aligned with OpenAI’s EHS standards and relevant specialists. - Translate applicable OSHA construction and general-industry requirements into practical site expectations, verify implementation and clarify responsibilities as work transitions from construction to commissioning and Operations. - Partner with site and discipline leaders to assess high-risk work, verify critical controls and escalate unsafe conditions, including electrical energization, hazardous energy, lifting, excavation and concurrent construction and operating activities. - Establish portfolio performance measures and reporting for HSE outcomes, contractor performance, corrective-action closure and handoff readiness; align definitions with delivery and Operations teams and validate data quality. - Lead cross-site performance reviews to identify recurring risks, compare execution against agreed expectations and drive improvement plans with accountable owners, milestones and follow-through. - Plan risk-based site assurance and contractor reviews, support incident and near-miss investigations, verify corrective actions and embed lessons learned across the portfolio. - Coordinate environmental compliance with site teams and specialists, including waste management, spill prevention, stormwater controls and relevant permit obligations. - Define HSE readiness criteria for operational handoff with commissioning and Operations teams, including training, procedures, emergency preparedness, outstanding risks and transfer of required records. - Provide clear portfolio updates and recommendations to leadership, surface decisions and resource needs early, and build consistent safety leadership across employees, developers, contractors and service providers. Qualifications - Substantial experience leading HSE programs for major construction or complex industrial projects, including oversight across multiple sites or workstreams and responsibility for contractor performance. - Working knowledge of applicable OSHA construction and general-industry standards, with experience translating requirements into site controls and verifying implementation across construction, commissioning and operating interfaces. - Practical understanding of data center or complex industrial hazards, including electrical safety, hazardous-energy control and high-risk construction activities. - Demonstrated ability to build assurance, performance reporting and corrective-action programs and use leading and lagging indicators to improve outcomes. - Experience coordinating contractors, site leaders and functional specialists through commissioning and operational handoff, with clear accountability across organizational boundaries. - Strong communication and judgment, with the ability to explain technical risk, influence leaders and field teams, and prioritize action in fast-changing environments. Preferred Skills - Experience with owner-side HSE oversight across a data center or mission-critical infrastructure portfolio, including developer-led and self-build delivery models. - Experience integrating environmental compliance, emergency preparedness and HSE management systems into construction and operational readiness programs. - Relevant professional credentials, such as CSP, CIH or an equivalent safety or environmental qualification, or comparable practical expertise. items.title: Network Infrastructure Lead
items.description: About the Role Lead OpenAI’s site network infrastructure delivery, coordinating the physical installation and readiness of network systems with the central network team and contracted installation providers. You will be OpenAI’s accountable on-site lead for physical network infrastructure construction and deployment, directing and overseeing the work of general contractors, specialist contractors and other service providers within your discipline. You will combine practical subject-matter depth with hands-on field leadership, managing contracted support to deliver safe, high-quality work to the integrated construction plan. Reporting and scope Report to the Site Construction Manager, who reports through the applicable project-management leadership. Maintain functional alignment with the Network Infrastructure leader and central network engineering team. Own day-to-day discipline execution and contractor performance within the assigned site scope and delegated authority. Coordinate priorities and interfaces through the Site Construction Manager; escalate material cost, schedule, design and acceptance decisions to the appropriate owners. This is a senior site delivery role, suited to an experienced superintendent, supervisor, manager or trade lead. Accountability is for an assigned discipline and site work packages. Site assignment, duration and any shared coverage follow project phase, workload and the staffing plan; effective on-site coverage is required during critical activities. Key Responsibilities - Manage structured-cabling contractors, fiber installers, network installation partners and other service providers against the site delivery plan. - Translate approved network designs into executable field packages and coordinate bills of materials, material availability and installation sequencing with the central network team. - Oversee pathways, duct banks and building-entry interfaces, fiber and copper cabling, racks, patching, labeling and network-equipment installation as applicable. - Direct fiber and cabling quality assurance, review test results and traceability, and drive correction of defective or incomplete installations. - Coordinate power, cooling, space and physical access readiness with electrical, mechanical and CSLA leads and hardware deployment teams. - Coordinate network provisioning, connectivity validation and handover with authorized network engineering and operations teams; maintain accurate installation and as-built records. - Set clear contractor deliverables and work priorities; review staffing, progress and quality, identify constraints early, and drive recovery actions through the Site Construction Manager. - Provide concise progress and risk reporting, evaluate field impacts of proposed changes, and maintain accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams. Qualifications - Typically 8–10 years of large-scale data center network deployment, structured cabling, physical-layer installation or infrastructure delivery, with demonstrated field and contractor leadership. Equivalent depth of practical delivery experience will be considered. - Strong understanding of physical data center network topologies, network components, bills of materials, rack constraints and installation sequencing; translate approved designs into executable field plans. - Deep practical knowledge of fiber and copper plant installation, trunks, panels, terminations, cleaning, labeling and cable administration, including routing diversity and pathway separation. - Ability to oversee and assess port-to-port verification, continuity, optical power and optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing; troubleshoot field installation and mapping discrepancies and verify remediation. - Experience defining contractor work packages and statements of work, evaluating delivery requirements, forecasting labor needs and tracking quality, throughput, cost drivers and schedule performance within delegated authority. - Experience coordinating deployment prerequisites with engineering and construction teams and completing formal operations handover with as-builts, port maps, test evidence and clear ownership transfer. - Comfort with ticket-based execution, change control, incident escalation and documentation workflows that make network installation repeatable and auditable. - Demonstrated ability to lead contractors and service providers through changing site conditions, set clear deliverables and acceptance criteria, and resolve performance gaps across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority. - Strong written and verbal communication: maintain accurate field records, action and decision logs, and explain technical risks, schedule impacts and recovery options to site leadership, engineers and delivery partners. - Sound judgment when information is incomplete: identify assumptions, prerequisites and interfaces, determine what work can proceed within approved authority, and escalate unresolved risks before they affect safety, quality or delivery. - Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated field leadership and subject-matter competence are central to this site role.
